classification.difficultyReason: Calculate one gradient, equate the gradients of parallel lines and solve for an unknown coordinate.

content.prompt: The line through the points $A(0,7)$ and $B(11,-6)$ is parallel to the line through the points $C(6,12)$ and $D(-11,d)$. Find the value of $d$.

answer.short:
$d=\dfrac{353}{11}$.

Use equal gradients for the parallel lines.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}m_{AB}&=\frac{-6-7}{11-0}\\m_{AB}&=-\frac{13}{11}\end{align*}$$
Parallel lines have equal gradients, so
$$\begin{align*}\frac{d-12}{-11-6}&=-\frac{13}{11}\\\frac{d-12}{-17}&=-\frac{13}{11}\\d-12&=\frac{221}{11}\\d&=12+\frac{221}{11}\\d&=\frac{353}{11}\end{align*}$$
